masked.report: Telegraph Fire Morning Update - June 10, 2021 (article 59686) and Evening Update - June 10, 2021 (article 59696)
masked.quote: Overnight, crews completed a burn out operation to secure complete protection of the Top-of-The-World community. [...] The burn out along Forest Road 651 is complete up to Sulphide Del Ray campground.
masked.reason: the only perimeter-extending events reported for the period are two burnouts (Top-of-the-World overnight; Forest Road 651 on the west side of Pinal Peak); the evening report describes only holding, patrolling and contingency-line work, with no natural fire advance. This plainly implies that most of the period's growth came from firing. Borderline: neither report gives acres or states the share explicitly

telegraph.note: Window from the NIROPS scans: 2021-06-05 20:59 to 2021-06-12 04:12 UTC (MST = UTC-7). The June 7 and June 11 reports (59639, 59704, 59729) describe the fire's own spread (active growth in dry grass/brush; moving east downhill from Signal Peak toward Pioneer Pass) and no firing. Full texts read 2026-10-26 from the build-Mac fetch.

masked.report: June 21, 2022 Pipeline/Haywire Fire Daily Update (covers June 20)
masked.quote: Yesterday, crews took advantage of the conditions and performed tactical firing operations in the northeast edge to tie the fire's edge into the Tunnel Fire burn scar to secure the outer edge of the fire.
masked.reason: the only perimeter-changing activity reported for the period; the same reports describe only interior heat and smoke otherwise (plainly implies the period's growth is from firing). Growth in the period is small (26,528 acres on June 20) and the interval is probably outside the evaluation window (90 % of the final area is reached by about June 16)
